method: Every CP003 violation and a sample of CP001/CP003 unknowns were manually inspected against the pinned workflow source. Classifications: TRUE_POSITIVE / FALSE_POSITIVE / UNKNOWN / NOT_ACTIONABLE.

cp001.classification: No strong (violated) unreachable claims were made on any real workflow, because 80.6% of workflows are partial (unsupported constructs), which correctly gates the strong claim. All 188 are UNKNOWN = NOT_ACTIONABLE (honest 'cannot determine'), not findings.
cp001.note: Zero false positives. CP001 currently produces no actionable strong findings on real repositories; this is correct-but-low-signal and is the main usefulness limitation for CP001.

violatedReviews.notes: actions/labeler; deliberate PRT+write, does not checkout fork code. Reachability claim is correct.
Carries a zizmor:ignore[dangerous-triggers] comment; CIProof names the specific reachable write job.
Workflow-level write inherited by job; base=master matched in counterexample.
Caller declares write; reusable internals unmodeled (limitation). Fork-reachable via 'closed'.
Guard reads PR as API data; job-level write reachable by fork.
Workflow-level write inherited by job (no job-level permissions).

cp003.unknownClassification: All 39 unknowns are ordinary pull_request + fork + explicit write, correctly reported UNKNOWN (fork-token downgrade depends on unmodeled repo settings). Zero were escalated to VIOLATED.
cp003.note: 10/10 violations are TRUE_POSITIVE; 0 false positives. Usefulness is mostly MEDIUM: these rediscover the known pull_request_target-with-write pattern, but with specific reachable-job + scope framing and a concrete counterexample.

cp002.policy: Explicit rules only; never inferred from job names.

rulesEvaluated.notes: on: release is unsupported; jobs never modeled -> not a useful test.
validate-tag-name always precedes linux; no bypass.

rulesEvaluated.rule: release requires dist; docker requires linux
rulesEvaluated.notes: prerequisites use matrix (unsupported) -> UNKNOWN, not a false violation.
skip_tests=true -> test SKIPPED, deploy RUN via always(); the intended CP002 counterexample.

forkGuardFalsePositiveCheck: Jobs gated on conditions CIProof cannot model (github.repository, github.actor, github.event.*) evaluate to UNKNOWN, not RUN, so CP003 never flags a fork-guarded job as VIOLATED. This false-positive class is structurally prevented and was not observed.
